sentences.text: Faecalibacterium prausnitzii is the most abundant bacterium of the human intestinal microbiota in healthy adults, representing over five percent of the bacterial population.
The species contains at least two phylogroups whose distribution differs between healthy subjects and patients with gut disorders.
Anti-inflammatory effects of the bacterium were shown in cell models and in chemically induced colitis in mice.
A reduced abundance has been reported in Crohn disease, where it was associated with higher risk of postoperative recurrence, and in other intestinal disorders.
